{{short description|Aspect of category theory in mathematics}}
In [[category theory]], a '''rig category''' (also known as '''bimonoidal category''' or '''2-rig''') is a category equipped with two [[monoidal category|monoidal structures]], one distributing over the other.

==Definition==

A rig category is given by a category <math>\mathbf C</math> equipped with:
* a [[symmetric monoidal category|symmetric monoidal structure]] <math>(\mathbf C, \oplus, O)</math> 
* a [[monoidal category|monoidal structure]] <math>(\mathbf C, \otimes, I)</math>
*  distributing natural isomorphisms: <math>\delta_{A,B,C} : A \otimes (B \oplus C) \simeq (A \otimes B) \oplus (A \otimes C)</math> and <math>\delta'_{A,B,C} : (A \oplus B) \otimes C \simeq (A \otimes C) \oplus (B \otimes C)</math>
* annihilating (or ''absorbing'') natural isomorphisms: <math>a_A : O \otimes A \simeq O</math> and <math>a'_A : A \otimes O \simeq O</math>

Those structures are required to satisfy a number of coherence conditions.<ref name="laplaza">{{Cite conference| doi = 10.1007/BFb0063106| isbn = 978-3-540-37270-7| pages = 281–375| last = Kelly| first = G. M.| title = Category Seminar| chapter = Coherence theorems for lax algebras and for distributive laws| series = Lecture Notes in Mathematics| date = 1974| volume = 420}}</ref><ref name="kelly">{{Cite book| publisher = Springer Berlin Heidelberg| isbn = 978-3-540-05963-9 | volume = 281| pages = 29–65| editor1 = G. M. Kelly| editor2 = M. Laplaza| editor3 = G. Lewis| editor4 = Saunders Mac Lane | last = Laplaza| first = Miguel L.| title = Coherence in Categories| chapter = Coherence for distributivity| series = Lecture Notes in Mathematics | accessdate = 2020-01-15| date = 1972| doi=10.1007/BFb0059555 |chapter-url=https://people.math.rochester.edu/faculty/doug/otherpapers/laplaza.pdf}}</ref>

==Examples==

* '''Set''', the [[category of sets]] with the disjoint union as <math>\oplus</math> and the cartesian product as <math>\otimes</math>. Such categories where the multiplicative monoidal structure is the categorical product and the additive monoidal structure is the coproduct are called [[distributive category|distributive categories]].
* '''Vect''', the [[category of vector spaces]] over a field, with the direct sum as <math>\oplus</math> and the tensor product as <math>\otimes</math>.

==Strictification==

Requiring all isomorphisms involved in the definition of a rig category to be strict does not give a useful definition, as it implies an equality <math>A \oplus B = B \oplus A</math> which signals a degenerate structure. However it is possible to turn most of the isomorphisms involved into equalities.<ref name="laplaza" />

A rig category is semi-strict if the two monoidal structures involved are strict, both of its annihilators are equalities and one of its distributors is an equality. Any rig category is equivalent to a semi-strict one.<ref name="guillou">{{Cite journal| last = Guillou| first = Bertrand| title = Strictification of categories weakly enriched in symmetric monoidal categories| arxiv = 0909.5270 | date = 2010 |journal=Theory and Applications of Categories |volume=24|issue=20|pages=564–579}}</ref>
